extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates / graduate students learning algebraic geometry and commutative algebra
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, theorems, and worked examples that build Spec A as a topological space with the Zariski topology and its structure sheaf OSpec A; includes localization, distinguished opens, stalks, local rings, radicals, and Krull dimension. Intended to teach how to compute sections and stalks and how algebraic properties correspond to topological features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spec A is the set of prime ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition 84.2.1: The set Spec A is defined as the set of prime ideals of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that Spec A includes non-maximal primes (generic/non-closed points) and not just maximal ideals; remark that (0) is prime iff A is an integral domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanishing locus and Zariski closed sets
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition 84.3.4: For f ∈ A, V(f) = {p ∈ Spec A | f ∈ p}; more generally V(I) = {p ∈ Spec A | I ⊆ p}. The Zariski topology on Spec A is declared by taking sets of the form V(I) as closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This algebraic definition of closed sets parallels affine varieties: closed sets correspond to ideals. Use V(I) notation and check that V(√I) = V(I).

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed points correspond to maximal ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: Question 84.3.6: A point (prime ideal) m ∈ Spec A is a closed point iff m is a maximal ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows one to recover the classical 'geometric' closed points inside Spec A as maximal ideals; closedness test by checking singleton closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguished open sets D(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition 85.2.1: For f ∈ A, D(f) = {p | f(p) ≠ 0} is a distinguished open set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguished opens are basic building blocks of the Zariski topology and are used to compute sections and stalks in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguished opens form a basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 85.2.2: The distinguished open sets D(f) form a basis for the Zariski topology: any open set U is a union of distinguished open sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof idea: if U is complement of V(I), then U = ∪_{f∈I} D(f). This basis property is crucial for computations via D(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections over D(f) are localizations A[1/f]
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 85.2.3: For A a ring and f ∈ A, OSpec A(D(f)) ≅ A[1/f].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives an explicit computation of the sheaf on distinguished opens; used to reduce general section computations to localizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global sections recover A
rubrics_metrics.description: Corollary 85.2.5: OSpec A(Spec A) = A (since Spec A = D(1) and A[1/1] = A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirms that Spec is the affine object whose ring of global functions is the original ring A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stalks of the structure sheaf are localizations Ap
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 85.3.1: For p ∈ Spec A, the stalk OSpec A,p ≅ A_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sheafification preserves stalks; germs (U, f/g) map to f/g in A_p. Use injectivity/surjectivity arguments with distinguished neighborhoods D(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stalks are local rings with unique maximal ideal pA_p
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 85.4.1: The localization A_p has exactly one maximal ideal, namely pA_p, so Spec A is a locally ringed space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize non-units: elements f/g with f ∈ p are non-units; any element not in pA_p is a unit (inverse g/f). This ideal captures 'germs vanishing at p'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residue field κ(p) = A_p / pA_p = Frac(A/p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 85.4.7 (germ-to-value square): κ(p) can be described as Frac(A/p); the diagram localize/mod out and then take fraction fields commutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice compute κ(p) as Frac(A/p); e.g., for maximal m, κ(m) ≅ A/m. This links enriched germs to ordinary values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization commutes with quotients
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 83.7.1: For multiplicative set S and ideal I, letting S̄ be image of S in A/I, S^{-1}(A/I) ≅ S^{-1}A / S^{-1}I where S^{-1}I = {x/s | x ∈ I, s ∈ S}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful algebraic fact used in proofs (e.g. germ-to-value square) and computations relating localizations and quotients; reference Atiyah–Macdonald for proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and behavior of generic / non-closed points
rubrics_metrics.description: Remarks and examples: non-maximal prime ideals correspond to non-closed (generic) points whose closures are irreducible closed sets; e.g. (0) in an integral domain is generic and lies in every open set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual intuition: generic points 'float' along their closed subset (the associated irreducible variety). Generic points simplify many topological arguments (e.g., irreducibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Irreducible spaces and closure-of-point correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition 84.3.9 and Theorem 84.3.14: X is irreducible iff it cannot be union of two proper closed subsets; for X = Spec A, points are in bijection with irreducible closed subsets (each irreducible closed set has a unique generic point).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use generic points to represent irreducible closed subsets; e.g., Spec of an integral domain is irreducible because (0) is in every open set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Krull dimension via chains of primes
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition 84.4.1: Krull dimension of A is supremum of lengths n of chains p0 ⊊ p1 ⊊ ... ⊊ pn of prime ideals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matches geometric intuition: C[x1,...,xn] has dimension n. Can equivalently define dimension of a topological space via chains of irreducible closed subsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radical and closed-set correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 84.5.1 and Theorem 84.5.5: V(√I) = V(I); √I = ∩_{p⊇I} p (radical is intersection of primes); V(I) = V(J) ⇔ √I = √J. Hence radical ideals correspond exactly to closed subsets of Spec A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric interpretation: √I is the set of functions vanishing on V(I). Proofs use localization and Krull's theorem (maximal ideals exist in localizations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nilradical characterization and reduced rings
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition 85.6.2 and Theorem 85.6.4: The nilradical p(0) (radical of 0) consists of nilpotent elements. Two functions f,g have same value at every p ∈ Spec A iff f − g is nilpotent. A is reduced iff nilradical is (0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows when pointwise values determine global functions: only guaranteed when A is reduced. Example: in C[x]/(x^2) many nonzero functions vanish at all points.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to compute general sections via distinguished opens and sheaf axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 85.2.iv and surrounding discussion: any open U is union of distinguished opens, and by using the sheaf axioms (pullback squares) one computes OX(U) by matching sections on a cover by distinguished opens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical recipe: cover U by D(f_i), compute A[1/f_i] for each, impose compatibility on overlaps A[1/(f_if_j)]. Example: punctured plane U = D(x) ∪ D(y) gives OX(U) = C[x,y] because intersection C[x,y,x^{-1}] ∩ C[x,y,y^{-1}] = C[x,y].

rubrics_metrics.name: Stalk-values relation: germs determine values
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 85.4 and examples: there is a natural map A_p → A_p / pA_p = κ(p) giving the 'value' of a germ; germs (enriched values) determine ordinary values via modding out by maximal ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the passage from local/germ perspective to pointwise evaluation; shows why computing in A or in A_p gives coherent results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local ring characterization via unit/test property
rubrics_metrics.description: Question/Problem 85C and commentary: A ring R is local iff for every x ∈ R either x or 1−x is a unit; in local rings non-units form the unique maximal ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives an alternate practical test for locality and explains why stalks are local by verifying unit condition in A_p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical computational recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Pedagogical guidance interspersed: prefer computing sections using distinguished opens and sheaf axioms rather than the 'useless' explicit sheafification definition; use Chapter 86 examples to build intuition; use localization and prime/prime-containment reasoning for proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly: define the presheaf F(U) = {f/g | g(p) ≠ 0 ∀p∈U} and sheafify if desired, but in practice compute OSpec A(D(f)) = A[1/f] and OSpec A,p = A_p. Consult Atiyah–Macdonald or Vakil for alternate constructions.
